# Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag — concept pack (small)

## How it works

- [statement] In the cryptocurrency volatility study, statistical significance changed with the chosen Markov order and could disappear at higher orders. The reported information-flow results also depend on binning and source/target block lengths. Lag and discretization sensitivity therefore belong in an uncertainty audit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9601717/
- [statement] Historical crypto information-flow direction should not be assumed permanent. Keskin and Aste explicitly warn that causation varied within their sample and that persistence is unproven; the daily-price leadership study likewise reports no definite information-transfer leader in its studied market. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8624574/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The deep-fusion study symmetrizes its directed adjacency matrix before embedding. Proposed implication: preserve the original directed graph separately when the task needs a leader-to-follower direction; symmetric asset similarity alone cannot retain that direction. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.02040

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] García-Medina and Hernández warn that general transfer-entropy causality analysis can produce spurious links through indirect effects or shared drivers. Proposed implication: require conditional rather than merely pairwise evidence for a claimed leader. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/
- [statement] Keskin and Aste found that adding histogram bins amplified both signal and noise. In their cryptocurrency sentiment analysis, quantile bins reduced the odd-versus-even bin sensitivity seen with equal-width bins; this is a study-specific estimation result rather than a universal bin-count rule. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/
- [statement] The multivariate cryptocurrency-network authors restrict their conclusions to hourly observations and describe their CoinMarketCap weighted, non-traded-price study as explanatory rather than predictive. These findings are not a direct validation of executable five-minute SOL forecasts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Keskin and Aste assess crypto information-transfer results with shuffled-series permutation tests and Z-scores. Their PyCausality repository demonstrates nonlinear transfer entropy with shuffling and significance output; this is evidence about dependency detection, not a probability of a profitable SOL trade. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag · also: https://github.com/ZacKeskin/PyCausality
- [statement] Keskin and Aste warn that overly fine histogram partitions bias transfer-entropy estimates in finite samples. Proposed implication: test binning sensitivity before using a nonlinear dependency score as a feature. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/
- [statement] A method called multivariate transfer entropy need not estimate nonlinear dependence: García-Medina and Hernández used jointly Gaussian conditional distributions, explicitly equivalent to linear Granger dependence. Their network findings therefore do not validate a nonlinear estimator. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/, https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.4514
- [statement] Schnoering and Inzirillo report cryptocurrency relationships at one-minute and five-minute sampling and describe the relationships as time varying. This is historical evidence of changing dependencies, not a verified present-day SOL forecast. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.02040
- [statement] The Kimchi-premium study warns that maximizing a transfer-entropy statistic across lags produces an upward-biased null maximum and optimistic significance. Proposed implication for a five-minute experiment: predefine the lag search and include lag selection in multiplicity control. Its empirical horizon is not a five-minute SOL validation. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/14/9/1501
- [statement] Bongiorno and Challet introduce time-shifted transfer entropy to locate information-transfer timescales, including where transfer peaks and disappears. Their stated application is stock-price ticks, so applying this method to SOL remains a research proposal. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.10173
- [statement] Transfer entropy measures directional statistical dependence by asking whether source history reduces uncertainty about the target beyond the target's own history. It can represent nonlinear dependencies; a symmetric association measure alone does not establish a leader. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/nlin/0001042 · keywords: Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/
- [statement] Raw histogram transfer entropy requires finite-sample uncertainty assessment: sparse counts and overly fine partitions can produce positive bias. A larger raw value alone is insufficient evidence of a stronger predictive relationship. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16215
- [statement] Effective transfer entropy subtracts a shuffled-series baseline from observed transfer entropy. This corrects an estimated null baseline; significance assessment additionally compares the observed value with the shuffled distribution. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8624574/ · keywords: Uncertainty-aware nonlinear crypto lead-lag · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/
- [statement] Bivariate transfer entropy can report an indirect link caused by a chain or a common driver. Conditional multivariate analysis evaluates a source in the context of other selected histories, but the conditioning set must be restricted to manage dimensionality. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/
- [statement] The cryptocurrency multivariate-network study uses maximum-statistic tests for candidate selection, minimum-statistic tests to prune redundant sources, and an omnibus collective test. These are explicit controls for repeated comparisons; choosing the largest unadjusted pairwise statistic is not the procedure studied. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/
